questions.question: Q1. Superelasticity in Nitinol occurs when the material is deformed at which temperature?

explanations.a: Incorrect — Below M_f, Nitinol exhibits the shape memory effect.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Below A_s, Nitinol is still in its martensitic state and exhibits shape memory.
explanations.c: Correct — Superelasticity is only observed at temperatures above A_f, where the stable austenite phase is stress-induced into martensite and immediately recovers upon unloading.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Superelasticity requires thermal activation above A_f.

questions.question: Q2. How does the electrical resistance of a Nitinol wire change during the phase transformation from Martensite to Austenite?

explanations.a: Incorrect — Martensite has a higher electrical resistivity than austenite.
explanations.b: Correct — Upon heating and transitioning to Austenite, Nitinol's electrical resistance drops by approximately 20%.
explanations.c: Incorrect — The phase change alters the electronic structure, causing a resistance drop.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Nitinol does not become a superconductor during this phase transition.

questions.question: Q3. According to the Coffin-Manson relation for SMA fatigue, what is the effect of doubling the applied strain amplitude?

answers.c: Decreases the fatigue life by a factor of 4 (inverse square)
answers.d: Decreases the fatigue life by a factor of 10

explanations.a: Incorrect — Higher strains decrease fatigue life.
explanations.c: Correct — Since fatigue life is inversely proportional to the square of strain (N = C / e²), doubling the strain decreases the cycle life by exactly 2² = 4 times.
explanations.d: Incorrect — The exponent is 2, not a base 10 logarithmic scaling.

questions.question: Q4. What is the maximum recoverable lattice strain (transformation strain limit) typically associated with binary Nitinol (Ni-Ti)?

explanations.a: Incorrect — Standard elastic metals recover <1% strain, but Nitinol is a superelastic alloy.
explanations.b: Correct — Nitinol can recover a maximum of 8% strain through reversible phase transformation before permanent slip occurs.
explanations.c: Incorrect — 25% strain exceeds the lattice transformation limits, leading to plastic damage.
explanations.d: Incorrect — 50% strain is far too high for metallic shape recovery.
